_about: exxeta-arm: SINGLE SOURCE of geometry, servo choices, mass estimates and options.
Everything else (CAD, URDF, kinematics, torque/power budgets, web 3D model) is generated from this file.
Units in this file: millimetres, grams, degrees, volts, amps (human-friendly). Code converts to SI.
Keys starting with '_' are comments and are ignored by all tools.
STATUS: sizing approved by the owner (Option B: 80/80 mm links, 50 g payload). See docs/decisions/ADR-0001.

design_targets._safety_factor_min: required torque <= rated stall torque at 6 V / safety_factor_min
design_targets._clone_torque_fraction: Information only: cheap clones often deliver 50-70 % of rated torque. The budget also prints the margin against this.

_about: Kinematic chain (SO-101 style): J1 base yaw -> J2 shoulder pitch -> J3 elbow pitch -> J4 wrist pitch -> J5 wrist roll -> J6 gripper.
TCP = grip centre between the jaws (not the fingertip end).
Reach = horizontal distance from the J1 axis to the TCP with the arm stretched out horizontally.
geometry._shoulder_height_mm: J2 axis above the table = base height + 1 + joint_design.shoulder_axis_above_turntable (the CAD checks this).
geometry._shoulder_offset_mm: Horizontal distance from the J1 axis to the J2 axis (0 = axes intersect).
geometry._wrist_to_tcp_mm: J4 axis to grip centre. Set by packaging: roll servo (~40 mm) + gripper plate + jaw pivot + jaw.

_about: Angle conventions (zero pose = arm pointing straight up, gripper up):
J1: 0 = forward, + = counter-clockwise seen from above.
J2: 0 = upper arm vertical, + = leaning forward.
J3: 0 = forearm in line with upper arm, + = bending forward/down.
J4: 0 = hand in line with forearm, + = bending forward/down.
J5: 0 = jaws open horizontally (when arm is horizontal), + = right-hand rule about the hand axis.
J6: 0 = closed, + = open (degrees of servo rotation; each finger moves pinion_radius x angle, see ADR-0006).
Ranges are preliminary (Phase 1 CAD sets the hard stops). Hobby servos give ~170 deg usable travel.
max_speed / max_accel are the DEFAULT conservative software caps (PROJECT_SPEC 10.7), not servo limits.

J5.name: wrist_roll
J5._pot: no J5 pot in v1 (owner decision, ADR-0002): keeps mass off the wrist

_about: Rated data from PROJECT_SPEC 4.2, cross-checked against datasheets (see docs/decisions/ADR-0001).
torque in kgf*cm, stall current in A at 6 V, idle current in A, body size L x W x H in mm (H includes output shaft).
spline_teeth MUST be re-checked on the purchased parts; we attach through the servo's own horn, so it is not critical.

MG90S._spline_teeth: sources disagree (20T or 21T, ~4.8 mm OD): count on the real part

_about: Mechanical dimensions of the servos and horns, in mm. Heights are measured from the BOTTOM of the servo case.
Clone servos differ by up to ~1 mm. MEASURE YOUR SERVOS with calipers and correct these before printing the final parts.
The single-joint test rig (Phase 1) exists to catch a wrong value here cheaply.

MG996R._shaft_offset: shaft axis to the nearer end of the body
MG996R._horn_face_h: bottom of case to the outer flat face of the metal round horn when mounted
MG996R._horn_pcd: 4 x M3 threaded holes on this pitch circle

MG90S._boss: round output boss on top of the case
MG90S._horn_top_h: bottom of case to the top face of the plastic horn when mounted
MG90S._horn: the double-arm plastic horn from the servo bag (arms at the top of the hub)

joint_design._about: Construction details of the joints (PROJECT_SPEC 4.3.1). All in mm.
joint_design._link_half_width: half width of every link in the direction perpendicular to link and joint axis
joint_design._gripper_pinion: rack-and-pinion parallel gripper: finger travel = pinion radius x servo angle
joint_design._horn_trim_len: the J5 and J6 double-arm horns are cut to this total length with side cutters

turntable._about: J1 bearing: printed four-point ball race (ADR-0004). Steel balls roll between two V-grooves.
turntable._ball_d: 6.0 mm steel balls. Bicycle balls of 1/4 inch (6.35) also work: change this value and re-export.
turntable._race_gap: radial gap between turntable and outer ring
turntable._race_clearance: extra room for the balls; preload is set with the clamp-ring screws and paper shims
turntable._cable_hole: cables pass through the turntable here, behind the shoulder

hardware._about: Catalogue masses of bought parts used in the mass model.

bearing_pitch._why: skateboard bearing: sold everywhere. One size on J2, J3 and J4 (ADR-0002).

pot.type: WH148 B10K, 6 mm D-shaft, 15 mm shaft

_about: Moving masses used by tools/torque_budget.py. Phase 0 = hand estimates (printed parts already include ~15 % contingency).
Phase 1 replaces every item with source 'estimate-print' by the CAD volume x density x fill factor (cad/export/masses.json).
Position along the stretched-out arm: 'from' = reference joint axis (J2, J3 or J4), then offset_mm and/or frac x that link's length.
Links: J2->J3 = upper_arm, J3->J4 = forearm, J4->TCP = hand.
An item belongs to the link that starts at its 'from' joint, unless 'link' says otherwise (e.g. the elbow servo body sits in the upper arm).
Items with source 'servo:Jn' take their mass from the servo assigned to that joint (mass_g is then only a reminder).
radius_from_roll_axis_mm (optional) = distance of the item's centre of mass from the J5 roll axis, for the J5 check.
cad_parts (added in Phase 1): names of the CAD parts that replace this estimate once cad/export/masses.json exists.
only_with_pots: item exists only when pots are fitted. The budget ALWAYS assumes pots fitted (worst case).

print._fill_factor: thin 3-4 mm walls with 3 perimeters are nearly solid

items.name: upper arm (printed fork + elbow servo cradle)
J3 servo MG996R (in upper arm, at elbow)
J3 passive bearing 608ZZ + pivot pin + M3 screw
cables along upper arm (4 servo + 1 pot lead)
forearm (printed fork + beam + wrist bearing stub)
J4 horn + passive bearing 608ZZ + pivot pin

payload._radius: assumed worst-case offset of the payload's centre of mass from the roll axis

friction_allowance_kgcm._about: bearing/cable drag allowance used in the J1 and J5 checks

base._about: Preliminary base data for the tipping check. Finalised by the base CAD (Phase 1/5).
base._foot_inset_mm: rubber feet sit this far in from each edge; the tipping line runs through two adjacent feet

stationary_cad_parts._about: once the CAD export exists, these entries of stationary_mass_items_g are replaced by the real part masses

power._about: Inputs for tools/power_budget.py. See docs/design/power_budget.md and the power ADRs.

pack._usable_fraction: energy we can use between the 8.2 V charge voltage and the 3.3 V/cell critical threshold

power._main_wire_awg: battery -> fuse -> switch -> converters. 16 AWG silicone wire carries well over 15 A; never thinner.

charger.adapter: 12 V DC, >= 2 A, 5.5 x 2.1 mm, EU plug (type C/F)

firmware_thresholds._about: Pack-voltage thresholds used by firmware and the safety node. Voltage is low-pass filtered so servo current spikes do not trigger them.

tolerances._about: Global print tolerances (PROJECT_SPEC 4.7). Tuned with the tolerance test print in Phase 1.

options._pot_shaft: D6 (6 mm D-shaft, default) | knurled6 (6 mm knurled/split shaft)
